items.question: A man and a woman are discussing a move to an open-plan office.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Did you hear that our company is moving to an open-plan office next month?

script.speaker: man
script.text: I did. Honestly, I think it's a good idea. People will talk to each other more, and ideas will spread much faster.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I'm not so sure. I need quiet to write my reports, and I can't concentrate when someone is on the phone next to me.

script.speaker: man
script.text: There will be a few small rooms for private calls, though.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: That helps, I suppose. What worries me more is that everyone will be watching everyone else. I'd feel under pressure all day.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I used to think that too, but at my last job nobody cared what anyone was doing. You get used to it within a week.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Maybe. And I suspect it's mostly about saving money. Fewer walls means less space to pay for.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Exactly, that's the real reason, of course. But if the savings pay for better coffee and more flexible hours, I won't complain.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Better coffee would certainly help. But I'd rather have a bigger say in decisions like this one.

script.speaker: man
script.text: You're right. They should have asked us before announcing it.

statements.text: Sharing one space makes it easier for ideas to travel between colleagues.

explanation.en: The man says people will talk more and ideas will spread faster. The woman never mentions this benefit.
explanation.es: Solo el hombre dice que la gente hablará más y las ideas se extenderán antes. La mujer no menciona esa ventaja.

statements.text: Noise from other people makes it hard to focus on writing.

explanation.en: The woman says she can't concentrate when someone is on the phone nearby. The man only mentions private rooms.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que no se concentra si alguien habla por teléfono cerca. El hombre solo habla de salas privadas.

statements.text: The main reason for the change is to cut costs.

explanation.en: The woman says it's mostly about saving money, and the man answers: "that's the real reason".
explanation.es: La mujer dice que es sobre todo por ahorrar y el hombre responde: "that's the real reason".

statements.text: Staff ought to have been consulted before the decision was made.

explanation.en: The woman wants a bigger say, and the man says "They should have asked us".
explanation.es: La mujer quiere opinar más y el hombre dice "They should have asked us".

items.question: A man and a woman are discussing homework for young children.

script.speaker: man
script.text: My son's school has stopped giving homework to the younger children. What do you think?

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I think that's a great decision. Children are tired after a full day, and they need time to play.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I'm not sure. Homework teaches them to organise their time, and that's a useful skill.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: But they're only seven or eight. They can learn that later.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Maybe you're right. I didn't have any homework until I was ten, and I turned out fine.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: There you are. But I do think children should read every evening, even if it isn't official homework.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Oh, I agree with that. Reading is the one thing I'd never skip. We read together every night.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: That's lovely. The problem is that some parents are too busy to help, so those children fall behind.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Perhaps, but I think most parents can find ten minutes a night.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Ten minutes is fine. It's the long worksheets I object to.

statements.text: Small children need free time more than extra work.

explanation.en: The woman says children are tired and need time to play. The man defends homework.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que los niños están cansados y necesitan jugar. El hombre defiende los deberes.

statements.text: Homework helps children learn to manage their time.

explanation.en: The man says homework teaches them to organise their time. The woman replies that they can learn that later.
explanation.es: El hombre dice que los deberes enseñan a organizar el tiempo. La mujer responde que pueden aprenderlo más tarde.

statements.text: Children should read at home every day.

explanation.en: The woman says children should read every evening, and the man says reading is the one thing he'd never skip.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que los niños deben leer cada tarde y el hombre dice que la lectura es lo único que no se saltaría.

statements.text: Some pupils may fall behind because their parents have no time to help.

explanation.en: The woman raises this problem. The man answers that most parents can find ten minutes a night.
explanation.es: La mujer plantea ese problema. El hombre responde que casi todos los padres encuentran diez minutos al día.

items.question: A man and a woman are discussing students using artificial intelligence to write.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I've noticed that more and more of my students let artificial intelligence draft their essays.

script.speaker: man
script.text: It doesn't surprise me. But is it really different from using a calculator? Nobody complains about that.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I'd say it is. A calculator does the arithmetic, but writing is how you work out what you actually think.

script.speaker: man
script.text: That's a fair distinction, although I'd argue that improving a machine's draft is a skill in itself.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Only if you can tell a good draft from a mediocre one, and that takes years of writing the hard way.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I used to dismiss that worry, but I've met graduates at my firm who can't structure a simple report without help. It's troubling.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: So you do see my point. Skills fade if people never practise them.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Partly. Where I disagree is banning the tools. Pupils will use them anyway, so schools should teach them to use them critically.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I wouldn't ban them outright either. But I'd insist on handwritten work in class, so there's at least a moment when they think unaided.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I'd rather schools taught pupils to use the tools well than to avoid them.

statements.text: Letting a machine write is much the same as using a calculator for sums.

explanation.en: The man makes the calculator comparison. The woman rejects it: "I'd say it is" different.
explanation.es: El hombre hace la comparación con la calculadora. La mujer la rechaza: "I'd say it is" different.

statements.text: Writing is a way of finding out your own ideas.

explanation.en: The woman says writing is how you work out what you think. The man talks about editing, not thinking.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que escribir es como descubres lo que piensas. El hombre habla de mejorar borradores, no de pensar.

statements.text: People's abilities can weaken if they depend on the tools.

explanation.en: The woman says skills fade without practice, and the man describes graduates who can't structure a report: "It's troubling".
explanation.es: La mujer dice que las habilidades se pierden sin práctica y el hombre describe a graduados que no saben estructurar un informe.

statements.text: Pupils should sometimes work without any technological help.

explanation.en: Only the woman asks for handwritten work in class. The man prefers teaching pupils to use the tools well.
explanation.es: Solo la mujer pide trabajo escrito a mano en clase. El hombre prefiere enseñar a usar bien las herramientas.
